scope: Q2k bounded ND/teaching ownership and explicit consumer audit

record.name: Teaching Dimension
record.definition: For $h\in\mathcal{H}$, a teaching set is a set of labeled instances on which no other member of $\mathcal{H}$ agrees with $h$. The **Teaching Dimension** is the maximum, over $h\in\mathcal{H}$, of the minimum size of such a set. For the empty class, set $\mathrm{TD}(\emptyset)=0$.
record.graph_summary: Largest, over concepts, of the minimum number of labeled examples that uniquely identifies the concept.
record.origin_references: The classical teaching-set model and teaching dimension originate in \cite{shinohara1991teachability,goldman1995complexity}.

monotonic.proof: For a target in a subfamily, every teaching set relative to the containing class is also a teaching set relative to the subfamily. Taking the target-wise minima and then the maximum shows that teaching dimension cannot increase on a subfamily.

c_monotonic.proof: For each target in the conditioned fibre, delete fixed coordinates from a teaching set in the original class.  It remains a teaching set in the fibre.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

p_monotonic.proof: Counterexample: $\mathcal H=\{001,010,100\}$ has teaching dimension 1, since each concept has a private positive coordinate. Projecting away the first coordinate gives $\{00,01,10\}$, whose every concept needs two coordinates to be identified, hence has teaching dimension 2.

record.name: Relative Hitting Size
record.definition: The **Relative Hitting Size** is $\max_{h\in\mathcal{H}}\mathrm{HT}(\{h'\mathbin{\triangle}h:h'\in\mathcal{H}\})$; equivalently, it is the maximum teaching-set size.
record.graph_summary: The worst hitting size after translating the class by one of its concepts.

monotonic.proof: Relative hitting size equals maximum teaching-set size (teaching dimension), which is monotonic under subfamilies by restricting each target's teaching set.

c_monotonic.proof: This is equal to maximum teaching-set size; the latter is c-monotonic by restricting each teaching set to the unfixed coordinates.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

p_monotonic.proof: Relative hitting size equals teaching dimension. The class $\{001,010,100\}$ has value 1, while projection away the first coordinate gives $\{00,01,10\}$, whose value is 2 by the teaching-dimension projection counterexample.

shared_goldman_citation_records.disposition: shared teaching-source citation; no ND antecedent in displayed record proof

record.name: Minimum Teaching Set Size
record.definition: The **Minimum Teaching Set Size** of $\mathcal{H}$ is $\min_{h\in\mathcal{H}}\operatorname{ts}(h,\mathcal{H})$, where $\operatorname{ts}(h,\mathcal{H})$ is the minimum size of a teaching set for $h$ in $\mathcal{H}$.
record.graph_summary: Smallest teaching-set size attained by a concept in the class.
record.origin_references: This is the minimum counterpart of the classical teaching-set framework of \cite{shinohara1991teachability,goldman1995complexity}.
record.comments: Not c-monotonic: $\mathcal H=\{000,001,010,100,110\}$ has minimum teaching-set size $1$, while conditioning the last coordinate to $0$ gives the full two-dimensional cube, whose minimum teaching-set size is $2$.

monotonic.proof: Counterexample: H={000,001,010,011,100} has minimum teaching-set size 1 because 100 is identified by one coordinate. Its subfamily {000,001,010,011} is the full two-cube and has minimum teaching-set size 2.

p_monotonic.proof: Counterexample: H={001,010,011,100} has minimum teaching-set size 1. A two-coordinate projection is the full two-cube {00,01,10,11}, whose minimum teaching-set size is 2.

c_monotonic.proof: Counterexample: H={000,001,010,100,110} has minimum teaching-set size 1; conditioning its last coordinate to 0 gives the full two-cube, whose minimum teaching-set size is 2.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

record.name: Maximum Teaching Set Size
record.definition: The **Maximum Teaching Set Size** of $\mathcal{H}$ is $\max_{h\in\mathcal{H}}\operatorname{ts}(h,\mathcal{H})$. It is the classical teaching dimension.
record.graph_summary: Largest minimum teaching-set size; equal to the teaching dimension.
record.origin_references: This is the classical teaching dimension of \cite{shinohara1991teachability,goldman1995complexity}.

monotonic.proof: A teaching set for a target remains a teaching set after restricting to a subfamily. Therefore every remaining target has no larger minimum teaching-set size, and taking their maximum cannot increase the value.

c_monotonic.proof: Restrict every target's teaching set to the unfixed coordinates.  The restricted sample still distinguishes the target within the conditioned fibre.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

p_monotonic.proof: This parameter is exactly equal to Teaching Dimension by the established relationship `teaching_dimension_maximum_teaching_set_size`; its p monotonic classification transfers unchanged.

record.witness_verification: For every n>=1, the full cube has positive teaching dimension infinity because its empty concept has no positive teaching set, while its ordinary teaching dimension is n. Thus the gap is unbounded.
record.name: Positive Teaching Dimension / Teaching Dimension
record.proof: Positive teaching sets are a restricted class of ordinary teaching sets.  Therefore the minimum teaching-set size for each target, and hence its worst case, cannot decrease under the positivity restriction.

record.details: A corner of a contained cube must be distinguished on every cube coordinate.
record.name: Maximum Teaching Set Size / Largest Strongly Shattered Set
record.proof: For a contained $d$-cube, choose any corner.  For each of the $d$ cube coordinates there is a neighbouring concept differing only there, so every teaching set for that corner must include all $d$ coordinates.  Thus the maximum teaching-set size is at least $d$.
record.witness_verification: For the family #classes/singletons_plus_empty_set with n>=4, the established endpoint values or bounds, in parameter order, are $n$ and $1$. The first parameter divided by one plus the second tends to infinity as n tends to infinity, ruling out every reverse affine-linear bound. See the database-owned value proofs for these two endpoints.

record.details: For every nonempty finite class, the stronger bound $\mathrm{TD}(\mathcal H)\leq|\mathcal H|-1$ holds.
record.proof: Fix $h\in\mathcal H$. For each other $h'\in\mathcal H$, choose one coordinate on which h and $h'$ differ. The union of these at most $|\mathcal H|-1$ coordinates is a teaching set for h. Maximize over h.

record.name: Teaching Dimension / No-Clashing Teaching Dimension
record.details: Every globally identifying teaching map is no-clashing.
record.proof: For each $h\in\mathcal H$, choose a teaching set $T(h)$ of size at most $\mathrm{TD}(\mathcal H)$. If $h\ne h'$, then $T(h)$ is inconsistent with $h'$ because it identifies $h$ uniquely in the whole class. Thus no pair can clash, and the same map witnesses $\mathrm{NCTD}(\mathcal H)\leq\mathrm{TD}(\mathcal H)$.
record.proof_source: Full proof in the LaTeX survey: Proposition prop:td-low-nctd.
record.witness_verification: For the $n$ singletons together with the empty concept, teaching dimension is $n$ while no-clashing teaching dimension is 1.

record.name: Teaching Dimension / Antichain Number

record.details: Relative hitting size is exactly the teaching dimension.
record.proof: For every target, a relative hitting set is precisely a teaching set for that target.  The established teaching dimension of Warmuth's $C_5$ class is three, hence its relative hitting size is three as well.

record.name: Teaching Dimension of Universal Class
record.proof: For each target $u_i$, the single labeled example $(\{i\},1)$ excludes every $u_j$ with j different from i. Since the class has at least two hypotheses, no empty sample identifies a target. Thus every target has minimum teaching-set size one.

shared_goldman_citation_records.disposition: shared teaching-source citation; no ND antecedent in displayed record proof

record.name: Minimum Teaching Set Size of Universal Class
record.proof: The one-point positive sample $(\{i\},1)$ teaches each $u_i$, because no other $u_j$ is positive at the domain point $\{i\}$. No target can be taught by the empty sample in a non-singleton class. Hence the minimum attained teaching-set size is one.

record.name: Maximum Teaching Set Size of Universal Class
record.proof: For every i, $(\{i\},1)$ is a teaching sample for $u_i$, while no empty sample distinguishes it from the other universal hypotheses. Thus every target has teaching-set size exactly one, and so does their maximum.

record.name: Relative Hitting Size of Universal Class
record.proof: For finite concept classes, relative hitting size equals teaching dimension. The universal class has teaching dimension one: $(\{i\},1)$ uniquely identifies each target $u_i$.

record.name: Maximum Teaching Set Size of Majority
record.proof: Maximum teaching-set size is at least maximum degree, whose established majority-class value is $n$. It is at most maximum projected teaching-set size, also $n$ on this class. Therefore it equals $n$.

record.name: Average Teaching Dimension of the Universal Class
record.proof: The established minimum teaching-set size and teaching dimension of the universal class are both one. Hence every individual minimum teaching-set size equals one, giving average teaching dimension one.
